transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I'm here because I've been suffering from an intense, overwhelming fear of enclosed spaces, particularly elevators, for about a year and two months now. It has become incredibly difficult for me to handle these situations.
When you're faced with an elevator or similar enclosed space, do you go out of your way to avoid it, or do you endure it with intense fear?

I do both, honestly. I actively avoid them whenever possible, like taking the stairs even if it means climbing many flights. But when I absolutely have to use one, I force myself to endure it while feeling an intense, overwhelming fear.
Do you experience physical symptoms like sweating, rapid heartbeat, or dizziness when you're in or even thinking about an enclosed space like an elevator?

Yes, I definitely do. My heart starts racing, I sweat, and I struggle to breathe whenever I have to get into an elevator. Even just thinking about having to use one later in the day triggers those same physical reactions.
